audit.why: Lane difficulty is stated as favoured 4/10 with Nautilus threat 5/10, matching the 49.54% enemy win rate and all-Lulu level chart.
Level 6 (Wild Growth) and first-item shield/Polymorph compounding are named as the power spikes, consistent with Lulu's kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never mentions that Nautilus's Q (Dredge Line) creates terrain and can pull him through walls to cut off Lulu's retreat, and Lulu has no dash to escape that. breakdown.cooldowns also carries no real cooldown number, only 'His only real engage'.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags rule terrain-cuts-retreat: Dredge Line colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus to it, letting him close gaps through walls that would otherwise block him; since Lulu's only escape tools are Q's slow and Flash, she must hold Flash specifically for that wall-pull rather than for the direct hook damage. The kit also gives Q's real cooldown as 14/13/12/11/10s.
audit.corrected: Add a Dredge Line/terrain warning to breakdown.cooldowns with real numbers, and a dosFull/dontsFull entry about not wasting Flash on the direct hook when the wall-pull is the actual retreat-cutting threat.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook): matchup-defining — His only real engage — dodge it and the lane is free. It writes your spacing rules. - W Whimsy is for saving fights, not seasoning trades. - The R opens or closes fights — pick one per cast.
edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook): 14/13/12/11/10s CD — his only real engage, and it drags him through terrain to reach you, cutting a retreat your dashless kit can't out-walk. Hold Flash for the wall-pull, not the direct hit. - W Whimsy is for saving fights, not seasoning trades. - The R opens or closes fights — pick one per cast.
Respect the wall-pull, not just the hook

edits.before: Q the doubled angle, E-mark the carry, auto — Pix volleys the chip while your buttons wait for the real question.
edits.after: Dredge Line pulls Nautilus through terrain toward whatever it hits — position so a landed hook doesn't also drag him past a wall that was your escape route.
Burn Flash on the hook's damage

edits.before: Polymorphing poke out of irritation and meeting the engage with a shrug — the W is the matchup.
edits.after: The hit itself is survivable with a shield; it's the terrain pull closing his gap that removes your retreat. Save Flash for that, not the initial poke.
